passages.where: Proverbs sets a person of many companions, who may come to ruin, beside a friend who stays closer than a brother. The site's note says the first line is difficult in Hebrew and translations differ, but the second is clear; the word for friend means one who loves, and the verb is the one used of a man holding fast to his wife and of Ruth clinging to Naomi. True friendship, the note says, is a matter of loyal love.

A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for adversity. The site's note calls these among the chapter's best known lines. Friendship is tested and shown not in the easy seasons but in the hard ones.

The wounds of a friend are faithful, but the kisses of an enemy deceive. The site's note says the chapter values honest friends and honest rebuke. A friend who never tells you a hard truth may be pleasant company, but Proverbs does not call that faithfulness.
As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another. The image is of friction that makes both blades better. Deep friendship is not only comfort; it is two lives shaping each other toward wisdom.

After watching a man who toils alone with no one to share his life, the Teacher praises companionship: two are better than one, because if one falls the other can lift him up. The site's note says he ends with a cord of three strands that is not quickly broken. Even the most skeptical book in the Bible counts friendship among the real goods of life under the sun.

When Job loses everything, three friends come and sit on the ground with him for seven days and nights without saying a word, because they see how great his suffering is. The site's note says they sat with him in silence. Later their speeches go badly wrong, but their first week of silent presence is the part of their friendship worth copying.

Four men carry a paralyzed friend to Jesus, cannot get through the crowd, and dig through the roof to lower him down. The site's note says their persistence is what Jesus calls faith, and that he speaks to the man because he sees the friends' faith. Sometimes a friend carries you to the place you could not reach yourself.

John states plainly that Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. The site's note says he places that love first so that what follows, a delay and then tears at the tomb, is read in its light. The Son of God had friends, and he wept with them.

Jesus says no one has greater love than this, that he lay down his life for his friends, and then calls his disciples friends rather than servants. The site's note says verse 13 defines the measure of the love he commands. The highest love Scripture names is spoken of friendship.

Writing from prison after many in Asia have deserted him, Paul thanks God for Onesiphorus, who often refreshed him, was not ashamed of his chains, and searched Rome until he found him. The site's plain note says that whatever else is uncertain about the verse, Paul's thankfulness for a friend who was not ashamed of him is plain. Some friendships are measured by who comes looking for you.

misread.taken: Bad company corrupts good character is often quoted as a rule that Christians should have no close friends who do not share their faith, or should drop friends who are struggling.
misread.says: The site's note says Paul is warning the Corinthians about voices inside the church who deny the resurrection and are corrupting the church's conduct. It is not a rule against friendship with people outside the faith: the site's note on 2 Corinthians 6 says believers are to be friends, neighbors, coworkers and good citizens with people of every faith and none, and Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners. The proverb is still true about companions who draw you into sin, as Proverbs says of walking with the wise or with fools, but it gives no one a reason to abandon a friend in trouble.

whole: Many adults find that real friendship becomes harder to keep just as they need it most. School and early jobs threw people together; then come moves, marriages, children, long hours and screens, and friendships thin out into group chats and occasional messages. Some people have many acquaintances and no one they could call at two in the morning. Some have been let down by friends and stopped trying. And churches, which ought to be the easiest place to find friends, can feel like rooms full of people who shake hands and go home.

Scripture takes friendship more seriously than most of us do. Proverbs praises the friend who stays closer than a brother, the one who loves at all times, the friend whose wounds are faithful and who sharpens like iron. Jesus had friends, loved them by name and wept with them, and he called the greatest love the laying down of life for friends. Part of why friendship is hard is that it costs what we are short of: time, attention, honesty and the willingness to be known. Part is fear. To be known is to risk being found out, and many of us would rather be admired at a distance than loved up close. Part is simply that friendship is never an efficient use of anyone's day, and we have arranged our lives around efficiency.

So the Bible's wisdom is to treat friendship as a love worth building on purpose. Make room for a few people, not only many acquaintances, and keep turning up for them over the years. Be the kind of friend Scripture describes: present in hard seasons, as Job's friends were for their first silent week; honest when honesty is costly; glad to sharpen and be sharpened; willing to carry a friend to Jesus when he cannot walk. Let yourself be known, starting small. Choose companions who make you wiser rather than ones who make wrong easier. Do not abandon friends who are struggling, and do not keep away from people who do not share your faith. Look in your church for people unlike you, older and younger, and eat with them.

The hope beneath this is that we were made for friendship by a God who is himself a communion of love, and who in Christ has called us friends. Jesus, who no longer calls his followers servants, lays down his life for them and does not leave them. Two are better than one, the Teacher said, and a cord of three strands is not quickly broken. Friendships in this life will disappoint us sometimes, and some will end. But no one who belongs to Christ is finally friendless, and every true friendship here is a foretaste of the one that will not end.
sit: Who would you call at two in the morning, and who would call you; and what would it take to become that kind of friend to one more person this year?

prayer.lead: A song of ascents about how good it is when brothers and sisters live together in harmony. Pray it for the friends you have and the ones you hope for.
